_note: Human-written inputs to the authoring agent for the 9 problems VerilogEval does not cover. Port names and widths match HDLBits so learners can reuse their HDLBits answers; all wording is our own. Review before running the agent.

module.outline: Instantiate the provided module mod_a once and connect it to the top-level ports.
module.given: module mod_a(input in1, input in2, output out)
module.given_behaviour_hint: Make mod_a non-commutative (for example out = in1 & ~in2) so swapped connections are caught.
module.top: module top_module(input a, input b, output out)

module_pos.outline: Instantiate mod_a and connect its ports by position: out1, out2, then a, b, c, d.
module_pos.given: module mod_a(output, output, input, input, input, input)
module_pos.given_behaviour_hint: Every input must affect the outputs differently so any misordered connection is caught.
module_pos.top: module top_module(input a, input b, input c, input d, output out1, output out2)

module_name.outline: Instantiate mod_a and connect its ports by name; mod_a declares its ports in a different order from top_module.
module_name.given: module mod_a(output out1, output out2, input in1, input in2, input in3, input in4)
module_name.given_behaviour_hint: Every input must affect the outputs differently so any misnamed connection is caught.
module_name.top: module top_module(input a, input b, input c, input d, output out1, output out2)

module_shift.outline: Chain three instances of the provided D flip-flop my_dff into a 3-stage shift register.
module_shift.given: module my_dff(input clk, input d, output q)
module_shift.top: module top_module(input clk, input d, output q)

module_shift8.outline: Chain three my_dff8 instances; sel picks how many clock cycles of delay reach q (0, 1, 2 or 3).
module_shift8.given: module my_dff8(input clk, input [7:0] d, output [7:0] q)
module_shift8.top: module top_module(input clk, input [7:0] d, input [1:0] sel, output [7:0] q)

module_add.outline: Build a 32-bit adder from two provided 16-bit adders; the low half's carry feeds the high half and the final carry is dropped.
module_add.given: module add16(input [15:0] a, input [15:0] b, input cin, output [15:0] sum, output cout)
module_add.top: module top_module(input [31:0] a, input [31:0] b, output [31:0] sum)
module_add.directed_hint: Include vectors where the low half carries out, e.g. a = 32'h0000FFFF, b = 1.

module_fadd.outline: Same 32-bit adder as module_add, but the learner also writes the 1-bit full adder add1 that the provided add16 is built from.
module_fadd.given: module add16(input [15:0] a, input [15:0] b, input cin, output [15:0] sum, output cout), built from 16 instances of the learner's add1
module_fadd.learner_writes: module add1(input a, input b, input cin, output sum, output cout)
module_fadd.top: module top_module(input [31:0] a, input [31:0] b, output [31:0] sum)

module_cseladd.outline: Build a 32-bit carry-select adder: one add16 for the low half, two add16 computing the high half with carry-in 0 and 1, and a 2-to-1 mux picking the high half by the low half's carry-out.
module_cseladd.given: module add16(input [15:0] a, input [15:0] b, input cin, output [15:0] sum, output cout)
module_cseladd.top: module top_module(input [31:0] a, input [31:0] b, output [31:0] sum)
module_cseladd.directed_hint: Include vectors where the low half carries out and where it does not.

module_addsub.outline: Build a 32-bit adder-subtractor from two add16: when sub is 1, invert b with XOR against sub replicated to 32 bits and feed sub in as the low carry-in.
module_addsub.given: module add16(input [15:0] a, input [15:0] b, input cin, output [15:0] sum, output cout)
module_addsub.top: module top_module(input [31:0] a, input [31:0] b, input sub, output [31:0] sum)
module_addsub.directed_hint: Must include a = 5, b = 3, sub = 1 (catches b ^ sub without replication: result 8 instead of 2), plus sub = 0 cases.
